name: Salesflare
summary: CRM for small B2B teams that auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar. Deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and basic reporting unless you export.
best_for: small B2B teams whose reps hate data entry — Salesflare auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar
skip_if: you need deep customisation, a big integration marketplace, or built-in calling and invoicing — Pipedrive or a fuller CRM fit better
honest_knock: It's deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and reporting feels basic unless you export. Integrations cover the essentials (Gmail, Outlook, Zapier) but niche tools lean on Zapier — and at higher seat counts the price overlaps fuller CRMs.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-14 and re-read unchanged 2026-09-27 on salesflare.com/pricing, per user a month) Three plans, and the page carries both billing terms plus a $/€ switch: Growth $39 a month or $29 billed annually, Pro $64 or $49, and Enterprise $124 or $99 with a minimum of five users. The euro column prints the same numerals — €39/€29, €64/€49, €124/€99 — so a European buyer pays the same figure in a different currency rather than a converted one. Our earlier reading called this “$29–99 per user” with Growth at about $29–39 and Pro at about $49. The range was right and the label was not: the low number in each pair is the annual rate and the high one is what month-to-month costs, and the five-seat floor on Enterprise never appeared. Lead credits are part of the ladder rather than an add-on — 5 on Growth, 100 on Pro, 250 on Enterprise. There is a 30-day free trial with no card. On that same page the vendor commits to no onboarding fees and to no caps on contacts, users, email templates, tracked emails, custom fields, workflows, dashboards or pipelines.
